content_voiceover: This table covers APL with variant translocations, a favorite board topic because it tests whether you know which variants respond to ATRA and which don't. PLZF dash RARA, from t eleven;seventeen at q two three;q twenty one point one, occurs in about one percent of APL and is classically refractory to ATRA, this is the single most important variant to remember. NPM dash RARA, from t five;seventeen, occurs in about zero point five percent and is responsive to ATRA therapy. NuMA dash RARA, from t eleven;seventeen at q thirteen;q twenty one point one, is also responsive to ATRA. STAT5B dash RARA, arising from an interstitial deletion of chromosome seventeen, is refractory to ATRA, similar to PLZF. Finally, BCOR dash RARA, from t X;seventeen at q eleven;q twenty one point one, has only been reported in a single case, and while initially clinically responsive to ATRA, that patient had several relapses despite standard chemotherapy plus ATRA. The key teaching point for exams: PLZF and STAT5B fusions are refractory to ATRA, while NPM and NuMA fusions remain ATRA responsive.
keypoints: PLZF dash RARA, t eleven;seventeen: refractory to ATRA, one percent prevalence
NPM dash RARA, t five;seventeen: responsive to ATRA
NuMA dash RARA, t eleven;seventeen q thirteen: responsive to ATRA
STAT5B dash RARA: refractory to ATRA
BCOR dash RARA: rare, initially responsive but relapsed
keypoint_voiceover: For variant APL translocations, remember PLZF dash RARA and STAT5B dash RARA are refractory to ATRA, while NPM dash RARA and NuMA dash RARA remain ATRA responsive. PLZF is the classic refractory variant tested on boards.
